footnotes: Visit information: Visit procedures may be conducted over more than 1 day if all activities are completed within the allowed visit tolerance period of each visit. Participants should not initiate first dose of study intervention or escalate study intervention until all required activities for that visit are complete.

Fasting visits: On all clinic visits, except PK only visits, remind participants to report to the site in a fasting condition. Fasting is defined as a period of approximately 8 hours without eating and drinking, except water, or performing any significant physical activity. Participants should not take their study intervention prior to the fasting visit. If a participant is adversely affected by the fasting condition, they are allowed to eat; however, specific study procedures need to be completed while fasting. If a participant attends a fasting visit in the non-fasting state, reschedule a visit to complete the required fasting activities within the allowable visit interval.

Screening: All screening activities must take place within the 35-day window. Participants should not attend Visit 3 until results from Visit 1 and Visit 2 are received and initial assessments of eligibility are completed. At Visit 2, screening laboratory results will be reviewed to confirm eligibility. At Visit 2 and randomization, all screening results will be reviewed to confirm eligibility. Baseline fundus photography should be evaluated by a qualified eye care professional once initial assessments of eligibility are completed. Fundus photographs obtained per the protocol requirements and within 90 days before Visit 2 may be used for eligibility determination. Assessment of results is required prior to randomization at Visit 3 to confirm eligibility for enrollment.

Visit 3 (randomization to treatment): Visit 3 should be scheduled as soon as all screening activities have been performed and results are available to assess eligibility. Participants will be randomly assigned to the treatment arms at Visit 3 and will receive their first dose of study intervention after completing all baseline assessments including labs.
Telehealth or remote visits: Telehealth visits may be by telephone or other technology.
PK only: The only procedure performed for these visits is PK sample collection.

Early discontinuation visits: ED visits will be completed by participants permanently discontinuing early from the study. These participants should also complete posttreatment follow-up visit(s). The SoA reflects the procedures that may occur during these visits. If the participant is discontinuing at the time of a scheduled visit, perform that visit as an ED visit. Participants who withdraw from the study after signing the informed consent but who have not taken a dose of study intervention do not need to complete ED procedures.

Unscheduled visits: An unscheduled visit may occur per investigator discretion for clinical oversight. The study site will determine if fasting status is needed prior to the visit. Concomitant medications, AEs, and endpoint events are required and should be recorded in the CRF.

Visit 801: A posttreatment safety follow-up visit will occur approximately 6 weeks following the last treatment period visit or final treatment visit. All participants are required to complete the safety follow-up visit. The SoA reflects the procedures that may occur during these visits.

Protocol Amendment (a) – nonsubstantial amendment addressing feedback from an internal safety committee. Changes made to Sections 5.2 (Exclusion Criteria), 6.9.1 (Initiation of new Antihyperglycemic Medications), 6.9.2 (Rescue Therapy for Severe, Persistent Hyperglycemia), and 6.9.3 (Prohibited Medications) to update insulin use guidance. data.name: Age requirement
data.text: Participant must be at least 18 years of age and of the legal age of consent in the jurisdiction in which the study is taking place at the time of signing the informed consent.

data.name: Type 2 diabetes diagnosis
data.text: Have a clinical diagnosis of T2D according to the World Health Organization (WHO) classification or other locally applicable standards for at least 6 months prior to screening (Visit 1), with HbA1c ≤10.0% (86 mmol/mol) at screening (Visit 1).

data.name: Stable T2D treatment
data.text: Are on stable treatment for T2D for at least 90 days prior to screening (Visit 1), consisting of either diet/exercise alone or up to 3 oral AHMs (excluding incretins). Note: DPP-4i are allowed.

data.name: BMI requirement
data.text: Have a BMI >27 kg/m2 at Visit 1. Note: In participants with limb amputation or limb loss, the investigator should reach out to the Lilly medical monitor for information regarding calculation of BMI.

data.name: Stable body weight
data.text: Have a stable body weight (<5% body weight change) for 90 days prior to screening at Visit 1.

data.name: History of unsuccessful dietary effort
data.text: Have a history of at least 1 self-reported unsuccessful dietary effort to reduce body weight.

data.name: Contraceptive requirements
data.text: IOCBP, INOCBP, and individuals AMAB who agree to abide by the reproductive and contraceptive requirements provided in Section 10.4. may participate in this trial. See Section 10.4 for definitions and additional requirements related to contraception. Note: Contraceptive use by participants should be consistent with local regulations regarding the methods of contraception for those participating in clinical studies. For the contraception requirements of this protocol, see Section 10.4.

data.name: Informed consent capability
data.text: Are capable of giving signed informed consent as described in Appendix 1, which includes compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the ICF and in this protocol.

data.name: Reliability and willingness to comply
data.text: Are reliable and willing to make themselves available for the duration of the study and attend required study visits, and are willing and able to follow study procedures as required, such as self-inject study intervention, store and take the provided study intervention as directed, maintain electronic study diary and paper log, complete the required questionnaires, and undergo DXA procedure. Note: if a person is unable to undergo the DXA due to physical limitations of the DXA machine, or because they have implants, hardware, or other foreign materials that may interfere with the scan according to the DXA manufacturer's specification, this will not be considered an exclusionary criterion. See Section 8.1.2 for further details.

data.name: Prior or planned surgical treatment for obesity
data.text: Have a prior or planned surgical treatment for obesity. Exception: The following are allowed if performed >1 year before screening (Visit 1): liposuction, cryolipolysis, or abdominoplasty.

data.name: Prior or planned endoscopic/device-based therapy for obesity
data.text: Have a prior or planned endoscopic procedure and/or device-based therapy for obesity, such as, but not limited to mucosal ablation, gastric artery embolization, laparoscopic adjustable gastric banding, intragastric balloon, or duodenal-jejunal endoluminal liner. Exception: Prior device-based therapy is acceptable if device removal was more than 6 months prior to screening (Visit 1).

data.name: Obesity induced by endocrinologic disorders or monogenetic/syndromic forms
data.text: Have obesity induced by other endocrinologic disorders, for example, Cushing Syndrome, or are diagnosed with monogenetic or syndromic forms of obesity, for example, Melanocortin 4 Receptor deficiency or Prader Willi Syndrome.

data.name: Type 1 diabetes or related conditions
data.text: Have type 1 diabetes mellitus, latent autoimmune diabetes, or history of ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar coma.

data.name: Severe hypoglycemia or hypoglycemia unawareness
data.text: Have had 1 or more episode of severe hypoglycemia and/or 1 or more episode of hypoglycemia unawareness within the 180 days prior to Visit 1. Note: Any participant that the investigator feels will not be able to communicate an understanding of hypoglycemic symptoms and the appropriate treatment of hypoglycemia should also be excluded.

data.name: High fasting glucose at screening
data.text: Have fasting glucose >270 mg/dL (>15.0 mmol/L) confirmed by the central laboratory at screening (Visit 1).

data.name: Recent use of prohibited antihyperglycemic medications
data.text: Have taken within 90 days before screening (Visit 1) any of the following AHMs: amylin analogs, GLP-1 receptor agonists, GIP/GLP receptor agonists, or insulin.

data.name: Current or planned treatment for diabetic retinopathy and/or macular edema
data.text: Are currently receiving or planning to receive treatment for diabetic retinopathy and/or macular edema, for example, laser photocoagulation or intravitreal injections of antivascular endothelial growth factor inhibitors. Note: All participants will have a baseline fundus photography assessment prior to randomization (Visit 3). Qualifying fundus photographs obtained within 90 days before Visit 1 may be used for eligibility determination. See Section 8.2.11.

data.name: Renal impairment
data.text: Have renal impairment measured as eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2, calculated by eGFRcr-cys formula as per Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration as determined by central laboratory during screening (Visit 1).

data.name: Significant active autoimmune abnormality
data.text: Have evidence of significant, active autoimmune abnormality, for example, lupus or rheumatoid arthritis, that, in the opinion of the investigator, is likely to require concurrent treatment with systemic glucocorticoids during the course of the study.

data.name: Recent acute myocardial infarction or cardiovascular event
data.text: Have had within 90 days prior to screening (Visit 1): acute myocardial infarction.

data.name: Primary Efficacy Objective
data.text: To demonstrate that eloralintide 3 mg, 6 mg and/or 9 mg QW is superior to placebo for change in body weight and percent change in body weight from baseline to Week 64

data.name: Key Secondary Objective - Pooled Eloralintide Lipids and Blood Pressure

data.text: Liver chemistry stopping criteria (Section 7.1.1) and hepatic safety monitoring criteria for study drug interruption or discontinuation (Section 8.2.9).

data.text: Insulin use for >=14 consecutive days is prohibited (Section 6.9.1).

data.description: Enrollment condition limiting proportion of AFAB participants
data.text: An upper limit of approximately 70% enrollment of AFAB participants will be used to ensure a sufficient number of AMAB participants.

data.name: Randomization Allocation Condition
data.description: Randomization ratio across arms
data.text: Approximately 1035 participants randomly assigned to placebo, eloralintide 1.5 mg, 3 mg, 6 mg, and 9 mg at a randomization ratio of 2:1:2:2:2.

data.name: No-Dose Withdrawal Condition
data.description: Condition exempting participants from ED procedures
data.text: Participants who withdraw from the study after signing informed consent but who have not taken a dose of study intervention do not need to complete ED procedures.

data.name: Unscheduled Visit Condition
data.description: Investigator discretion triggers an unscheduled visit
data.text: An unscheduled visit may occur per investigator discretion for clinical oversight; the study site will determine if fasting status is needed prior to the visit. Concomitant medications, AEs, and endpoint events are required and should be recorded in the CRF.

data.name: Screening to Treatment (Randomization) Transition
data.text: After an up to 35-day screening period (Visit 1 to Visit 3), participants meeting all eligibility criteria (including PHQ-9 <15 at Visit 3, central lab fasting glucose <=270 mg/dL, eGFR >=30 mL/min/1.73 m2, and baseline fundus photography completed prior to randomization) are randomized 2:1:2:2:2 to placebo or eloralintide 1.5/3/6/9 mg SC QW.

data.name: Dose Escalation to Maintenance Transition
data.text: Following the 12-week dose-escalation period (stepping through 3 mg, 6 mg, and 9 mg every 4 weeks), participants enter the 52-week treatment maintenance period at their randomly assigned final dose.

data.name: Treatment to Post-treatment Follow-up Transition
data.text: After completion of the 64-week treatment period, participants enter a 6-week posttreatment follow-up period; Visit 801 occurs approximately 6 weeks following the last treatment period visit or final treatment visit and is required for all participants.

data.name: Dose Escalation Stepping Rule
data.text: To reach the doses of 3 mg, 6 mg, and 9 mg QW, a dose-escalation regimen stepping through each of these doses every 4 weeks will be employed.

data.name: Dose Modification for Tolerability/Safety
data.text: Dose modification (Section 6.6) may be applied for intestinal symptoms, inadequate nutrition or dehydration, BMI <=22 kg/m2, or perceived excessive weight reduction.

data.name: Rescue Therapy for Severe, Persistent Hyperglycemia
data.text: Participants must continue administering assigned study intervention unless insulin is used as short-term rescue therapy. Urgent use of short-term insulin in a hospital or closely monitored setting may be used as rescue therapy for severe, persistent hyperglycemia; insulin use for >=14 consecutive days is prohibited.

data.name: Temporary Study Intervention Interruption
data.text: Temporary study intervention interruption may be required per Section 7.1.2 and hepatic safety monitoring criteria (Section 8.2.9).

data.name: Discontinuation of Study Intervention for Liver Chemistry
data.text: Liver chemistry stopping criteria (Section 7.1.1) require permanent discontinuation of study intervention; hepatic safety monitoring criteria define study drug interruption or discontinuation.

data.name: Discontinuation of Study Intervention
data.text: Study intervention may be permanently discontinued per Section 7.1; participants permanently discontinuing early from the study complete Early Discontinuation (ED) visit procedures and should also complete posttreatment follow-up visit(s).

data.name: Scheduled Visit Converted to ED Visit
data.text: If the participant is discontinuing at the time of a scheduled visit, perform that visit as an ED visit.

data.name: Participant Withdrawal from Study
data.text: Participant discontinuation/withdrawal from the study per Section 7.2.

data.name: Prohibited Medication Initiation Rule
data.text: Initiation of prohibited medications, prohibited antihyperglycemic medications, prohibited surgical treatments/procedures or medications for weight management (Sections 6.9.1, 6.9.3, 6.9.4) is not permitted during the study.

data.name: Early Discontinuation (ED) Visit
data.description: ED visits will be completed by participants permanently discontinuing early from the study; these participants should also complete posttreatment follow-up visit(s). If discontinuing at the time of a scheduled visit, perform that visit as an ED visit.

data.name: Withdrawal Prior to First Dose
data.description: Participants who withdraw from the study after signing the informed consent but who have not taken a dose of study intervention do not need to complete ED procedures.

data.name: Lost to Follow-up
data.description: Participant lost to follow up per Section 7.3.

data.name: Study Completion
data.description: Completion of up to 35-day screening, 64 weeks of treatment (12-week dose escalation plus 52-week maintenance), and the 6-week posttreatment follow-up including the required Visit 801 safety follow-up visit approximately 6 weeks after the last treatment visit.

data.name: Screen Failure
data.description: Failure to meet eligibility criteria during the up to 35-day screening period (Visit 1 to Visit 3), e.g., fasting glucose >270 mg/dL, eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2, or PHQ-9 >=15 at Visit 1 or Visit 3.

data.name: Randomization Eligibility Decision
data.description: At Visit 3 (within 35 days of Visit 1), eligibility is confirmed (including repeat PHQ-9 and baseline fundus photography) and participants are randomized 2:1:2:2:2 to placebo or eloralintide 1.5/3/6/9 mg.

data.name: Dose Escalation Step Decision (Every 4 Weeks)
data.description: Every 4 weeks during the 12-week dose-escalation period, dose is stepped up to the next level (3 mg, 6 mg, 9 mg) unless tolerability/safety management criteria require dose modification.

data.name: Glycemic Rescue Decision
data.description: During treatment visits (every 4 to 12 weeks) and via self-monitoring of blood glucose, severe persistent hyperglycemia triggers rescue therapy decisions while continuing assigned study intervention unless short-term insulin is used.

data.name: Hepatic Safety Interruption/Discontinuation Decision
data.description: Liver chemistry results are evaluated against stopping criteria to determine temporary interruption or permanent discontinuation of study intervention.

data.name: Posttreatment Follow-up Decision (Visit 801)
data.description: Approximately 6 weeks after the last treatment period visit or final treatment visit, all participants complete the required safety follow-up visit; effects of study intervention cessation are assessed during this 6-week period.
